note: What people notice about a figure at a glance, and what town residents say about it. Presentation and flavour only: a salience tag never changes a disposition, a price, a roll or a number. Tags are derived from public appearance, equipped items' presentation blocks and visible condition, so every new item is noticed without being listed here.

how_to_extend.rules: Each rule is {tag, label, weight, any: [condition, ...]}; the rule fires when ANY condition matches. Conditions: {"gear": {key: value}} matches an equipped (or costume) item's presentation block, every key must match and a list means any-of (for `fx`, the value must appear in the item's fx list); {"appearance": {field: id-or-list}} matches the creator option id; {"colour": {"field": f, "family": family-or-list}} matches the hue family of a colour field (red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, white, grey, black); {"race": id-or-list}; {"age": "child"}; {"hp_below": fraction}. Higher weight is noticed first; at most max_tags are kept.
how_to_extend.reactions: reactions[tag] maps a resident class (floor_one_life.json `class`: townsfolk, trader, guard, labourer, clergy, bandit, goblin, child) or `default` to a list of lines. {name} is the resident, {lead} the figure being noticed, {label} the tag's label. A line is chosen from a stable hash, so the same resident says the same thing about the same look.
how_to_extend.verify: tests/test_looks_and_salience.py; the Actor Lab (/web/actor-lab.html) shows the client's read of a look.
how_to_extend.champions: Champion identity -> tags always noticed on them. Restate only what that champion's rig already draws from its canon design locks (web/doran-rig.js, web/wren-rig.js header comments); add nothing new about a canon character here.

rules.label: a weapon that smokes with rot
a weapon that hums with weather

default: {name} looks at the blood on you first and the face second.
{name} steps closer, then thinks about who did that to you and steps back.
clergy: {name} is already reaching for clean linen before you say a word.
guard: {name} asks who you were fighting, and whether they are still breathing.
child: {name} stares at the blood and goes very quiet.

default: {name} talks to the visor, since there is no face to talk to.
{name} waits a beat, as if expecting the helm to come off.
guard: {name} keeps a hand near the whistle until you speak.
child: {name} knocks on the air in front of your helm and grins.

default: {name}'s eyes keep sliding back to the glow of your gear.
{name} lowers their voice, the way people do near something old and valuable.
trader: {name} names a price for your gear before you have said hello.
{name} is doing sums behind their eyes, and the answer is large.
bandit: {name} takes a long, careful look at your gear, and then does not look again.

default: {name} steps back from your blade, the way you step back from a hearth that is too high.
townsfolk: {name} glances at the thatch overhead, then at your weapon.

default: {name} rubs their arms without meaning to.
{name} squints into the light off your gear.
clergy: {name} bows their head a fraction before they catch themselves.
bandit: {name} would rather you took that light somewhere else.

default: {name} wrinkles their nose at the rot-smoke off your weapon.
{name} keeps the well between you and that weapon.
clergy: {name} makes a small warding sign at your blade.

default: {name} watches the glow on your gear the way you watch a dog you do not know.
{name} looks up, half-expecting rain.
{name} hears you coming well before you arrive.
{name} sizes up the plate and decides to be polite.
guard: {name} straightens a little. Plate like that usually means someone important is paying.
labourer: {name} wonders aloud who has to carry all that when you fall over.

default: {name} checks their purse, then checks it again.
{name} speaks slowly and a little too loudly.
goblin: {name} flashes you a quick, conspiratorial grin.
guard: {name} watches your hands the whole time.

default: {name} gives your weapon the kind of room you give a cart horse.
guard: {name} asks, politely, that you keep that thing peace-bonded in town.

default: {name} reads the paint on your face and decides not to ask.
bandit: {name} nods at the paint like it is a password.

default: {name} has to tilt their head back to meet your eyes.
child: {name} asks if you can lift a whole cart. It is a real question.

default: {name} tries to get a look under your hood.
{name} speaks to the shadow where your face should be.
guard: {name} asks you to lower the hood. It is not quite a request.
bandit: {name} approves of the hood without saying so.

default: {name} steps into the circle of your lantern light.
child: {name} follows the lantern light with their whole face.

default: {name} notices the mark at your temple.
clergy: {name} asks, quietly, which shrine gave you that mark.

default: {name} hears the mail shift as you move.
guard: {name} gives your mail a professional once-over.

default: {name}'s eyes go to the scar, then politely away.
guard: {name} asks where you earned the scar.

default: {name} keeps an eye on the point of your spear.
{name} notes the bow and does not stand in front of you.
{name} glances at the staff and wonders what it is for.
clergy: {name} asks what the staff is carved from.

default: {name} wonders what the circlet means, and whether they should bow.
{name} notes the shield and the colours painted on it.
{name} takes you for some kind of scholar, or worse, a priest.
clergy: {name} studies the cut of your robes for a moment.

default: {name} steps aside to let you through a door that suddenly looks small.
{name} remembers the red hair, which is going to make you easy to describe later.
{name} will remember those colours.
trader: {name} wants to know who dyed that cloth, and what they charge.

default: {name} catches sight of your ears and looks again.
{name} looks around for whoever is meant to be watching you.
{name} follows the little stars circling your head and forgets what they were saying.
{name} squints at the crown of stars, trying to decide if it is a trick.
clergy: {name} goes very still under the light of your crown.
child: {name} tries to count the stars over your head, twice.
